pages.text: GOVERNMENT PORTALS

[Type here]


            Ministry of Education

YUKTI Portal

   •  YUKTI stands for Young India Combating COVID with Knowledge, Technology and
       Innovation.
   •  Objective: To monitor and record the efforts and initiatives of the Ministry of Education
      taken in the wake of COVID-19 Pandemic.
   •  Launch: April 2020.
   •    It covers the various initiatives and efforts of the institutions in academics, research
       especially related to COVID, social initiatives by institutions and the measures taken for the
      betterment of the total wellbeing of the students
   •    It allowed various institutions to share their strategies for various challenges aroused due to
     COVID-19 and other future initiatives.

           YUKTI 2.0
                 •  Objective: To help systematically assimilate technologies having
                   commercial potential and information related to incubated startups in higher
                    education institutions.
                 •  Launch: June 2020
                     ▪    It is an extension of earlier version of ‘YUKTI’.
                 •    It will help in fostering the culture of innovation and entrepreneurship in
                  academic institutions.

SPARC Portal

   •  SPARC stands for Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration.
   •  Launch Year: 2018.
   •  The portal was launched for implementation of SPARC Scheme.
   • SPARC Scheme Objective: To improve the research ecosystem of India’s higher
      educational institutions by facilitating academic and research collaborations between Indian
        Institutions and the best institutions in the world.

IMPRESS Portal

   •  IMPRESS stands for Impactful Policy Research in Social Science.
   •  Launch Year: 2018
   •  The portal was launched for implementation of IMPRESS Scheme.
   •  IMPRESS Scheme
      ▪  Objective: To encourage social science research in policy relevant areas so as to
         provide vital inputs in policy-formulation, implementation and evaluation.
      ▪  Implementing agency: Indian Council of Social Science Research.
      ▪    It seeks to encourage policy research in social sciences is to have visible impact on
            polity, economy, society, culture, media, governance, health, environment, technology,
         law etc.
                                                                                                                         pg. 5

[Type here]


ShaGun Portal

   •  Term ShaGun has been coined from the words ‘Shala’ meaning Schools and ‘Gunvatta’
     meaning Quality, signifying this twin track approach.
   •  Objective: To capture and showcase innovations and progress in Elementary Education
       sector of India by continuous monitoring of the flagship scheme-Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.
      ▪  SSA is a centrally sponsored scheme providing universal access to education to
          children in the age group of 6 to 14 years of age.
   •  Launch Year: 2017.
   •    It will help monitor progress of implementation of SSA by assessing performance of States
     and UTs on key parameters.
   •    It will serve as a platform for the central government for effective planning and deliver on
      the promise of providing quality education to all.
   •  Twin track approach of ShaGun:
      ▪  Repository: It focuses on positive stories and developments in the field of School
         Education.
      ▪    It displays state-level innovations and success stories that are driving improvements in
         performance under SSA.
      ▪    It has a decentralized management structure that enables State governments to choose,
         upload and manage their own content.
      ▪  Online monitoring module: It measures state-level performance and progress against
         key educational indicators.
      ▪    It collects and reports data which enables government and administrators to track
           efficiency with which SSA funds being utilized and the results it is delivering.

SWAYAM Portal

   • SWAYAM stands for Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds.
   •    It is World’s Largest Online Free E-Learning Platform Portal.
   •  Objectives:
       ▪  To take the best teaching learning resources to all, including the most disadvantaged.
       ▪  To achieve three cardinal principles of Education Policy viz. access, equity and quality
   •  Launch Year: 2016
   •  Developed by: All India Council for Technical Education
   •    It is Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) Platform for hosting of online courses which
      could be accessed by anyone, anywhere at any time free of cost.
   •    It covers subjects from high school onwards till higher education including Skill based
      courses to ensure that every student benefit from learning material through ICT.

DIKSHA Portal

   •  DIKSHA stands for Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing.
   •  Objective: To enable access to digital learning for students and teachers irrespective of
        their socio-economic backgrounds.
   •  Launch Year: 2017
   •  Developed by: National Council for Educational Research and Training.

                                                                                                                         pg. 6

[Type here]



   •    It is in the form of a free mobile application and web portal available for use anywhere,
      anytime and for anyone.
   •    It offers engaging learning material, relevant to the prescribed school curriculum, to
       teachers, students and parents.
   •    It provides quality e-content for school education in States/UTs and QR coded Energized
      Textbooks for all grades (one nation, one digital platform).

Kartavya Portal

   •  Launch Year: 2019 (On the occasion of ‘Constitution Day’)
   •    It was launched as a part of Nagrik Kartavya Paalan Abhiyan.
       ▪  Nagrik Kartavya Paalan Abhiyan was aimed at creating mass awareness about
        Fundamental Duties as enshrined in our Constitution.
   •    It was used primarily for holding monthly essay competitions for students as well as other
        activities like quizzes, debates, poster making etc pertaining to the Abhiyan.

SHREYAS Portal

   •  SHREYAS stands for Scheme for Higher Education Youth in Apprenticeship and Skills
   •  Launch Year: 2019.
       ▪    It was launched for implementation of SHREYAS Scheme.
   •    It will enable educational institutions and industry to log in and provide their respective
     demand and supply of apprenticeship.

     SHREYAS Scheme
           •    It was launched for providing industry apprenticeship opportunities to
              general graduates exiting in April 2019 through National Apprenticeship
             Promotional Scheme (NAPS).

              Ministry of AYUSH

NAMASTE Portal

   •  NAMASTE stands for National AYUSH Morbidity & Standardized Terminologies.
   •    It is a comprehensive web-portal for Standardized Terminologies and National Morbidity
     Codes of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani (AUS) Systems of Medicine and WHO-ICD-10/11.
           •  ICD stands for International Classification of Diseases. It is developed and
              annually updated by the World Health Organization (WHO).
           •  ICD-11 (came into effect from 1 January 2022) is the eleventh revision of
              the ICD.
           •    It has replaced the ICD-10 as the global standard for recording health
              information and causes of death.





                                                                                                                         pg. 7

[Type here]



Objectives:
      ▪  Pan India implementation of ASU National Morbidity Codes for reporting morbidity and
         treatment outcome along with ICD-10/11.
      ▪  Pan India Implementation of ICD-10/11 Disease Codes for Yoga, Naturopathy and
        Homoeopathy Systems of Medicine for reporting morbidity and treatment outcome.
      ▪  Serve as reference repository of A-S-U terminologies and Morbidity Codes for further
         development of A-S-U international terminologies and ICD-11 morbidity Codes.
   •  Launch Year: 2016
   •  Developed by: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences.

e-AUSHADHI portal

    •  AUSHADHI stands for Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy Automated Drug Help
         Initiative.
    •  Objective: Online licensing of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy drugs and
       related matters.
    •  Launch Year: 2019.
    •    It provides real time information of licensed manufacturers and their products, cancelled
      and spurious drugs, contact details of the concerned authority for specific grievances.
    •    It aids licensing authority, manufactures and consumers.
    •    It helps increasing transparency, improved information management facility, improved data
        usability and increased accountability.

 Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

SAGE Portal

   • SAGE stands for Seniorcare Aging Growth Engine.
   •    It is a “one-stop access” of elderly care products and services by credible start-ups.
   •  Elderly care products include life supporting devices, legal aid, housing facilities, financial
       support, food and nutritional support etc.
   •  Launch Year: 2021.
   •  Under it, start-ups are selected on the basis of innovative products and services.

Sacred Portal

   •  Sacred stands for Senior Able Citizens for Re Employment in Dignity.
   •  Objective: To devise ways to ensure Senior Citizens live healthy, happy, empowered,
       dignified and self-reliant life
   •  Launch Year: 2021.
   •    It brings the employment seeker senior citizens and employment providers on one platform.





                                                                                                                         pg. 8

[Type here]


TAPAS Portal

   •  TAPAS stands for Training for Augmenting Productivity and Services.
   •    It is the Online Learning Management Platform.
   •  Objectives:
      ▪  To provide access to lectures by subject experts, study material that supplements the
          physical classroom without compromising on the quality of teaching.
      ▪  To impart training and enhance the knowledge and skills for the capacity building of the
           participants.
   •  Launch Year: 2021.
   •  Developed by: National Institute of Social Defence, Ministry of Social Justice and
     Empowerment.
   •    It offers self-paced Online certificate courses in the key areas of Social Defence -Elderly
       care, Substance (Drug) Abuse prevention and Transgender issues.

PM-DAKSH Portal

   •  PM-DAKSH stands for Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi.
   •  Objective: To make the skill development schemes accessible to the target groups.
   •  Launch Year: 2021
   •  Developed by: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in collaboration with National
      e-Governance Division (NeGD), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).
   •    It provides all information related to skill development at one place for Scheduled Castes,
     Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis

           Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH)
            Yojana
                 •    It is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
                   from the year 2020-21.
                 •  Under it, eligible target group are being provided skill development
                       training programmes on
                    ▪   Up-skilling/Re-skilling.
                    ▪  Short Term Training Programme.
                    ▪  Long Term Training Programme.
                    ▪  Entrepreneurship Development Program.
                 •  These training programs are being implemented through
                 Government Training Institutes, Sector Skill Councils constituted by
                      Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and other the
                     credible institutions.





                                                                                                                         pg. 9

[Type here]


National Portal for Transgender Persons

   •  Launch Year: 2020.
   •    It enables any Transgender applicant to obtain Certificate of Identity and Identity Card
       without any physical interface with the office of issue.
   •    It helps a transgender person to apply for Certificate and Identity card digitally from
      anywhere in the country.
   •    It provides for the procedure for identification certificates issued by the District Magistrate
   •    It has been established and is functional in all districts of the country.

     Ministry of Commerce and Industry

SWAYATT

   •  Objective: To promote Start-ups, Women and Youth Advantage through e-Transactions on
     Government e Marketplace (GeM).
   •  Launch Year: 2019.
   •    It brings together the key stakeholders within the Indian entrepreneurial ecosystem to GeM,
      the national procurement portal.

Start-Up Portal

   •  Objective: To serve as the single platform for Start-ups for interacting with Government
     and Regulatory Institutions for all business needs and information exchange among various
       stakeholders.
   •    It acts as a one stop solution for all queries related to the Start-up India initiative.

Womaniya on GeM

   •  Objective: To develop women entrepreneurship on the margins of society to achieve
       gender-inclusive economic growth.
   •  Launch Year: 2019.
   •    It enables women entrepreneurs and women self-help groups to sell their products directly
       to various Government ministries, departments and institutions.

ARTIS Portal

   •  ARTIS stands for Application for Remedies in Trade for Indian industry and other
      Stakeholders.
   •  Objective: To facilitate online filing of applications for trade remedies.
   •  Launching Agency: Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR).
      ▪ DGTR is investigation arm of the Commerce Ministry which deals with anti-dumping
          duty, safeguard duty, and countervailing duty.
   •  Launch Year: 2019.

                                                                                                                        pg. 10

[Type here]



   •    It provides for filing of applications, responses and other related submissions with respect to
       various trade remedial measures.

MAARG portal

   • MAARG stands for Mentorship, Advisory, Assistance, Resilience and Growth.
   •  Objectives:
      ▪  To provide sector focused guidance, handholding, and support to startups throughout
           their lifecycle.
      ▪  To establish a formalized and structured platform that facilitates intelligent matchmaking
        between the mentors and their respective mentees.
      ▪  To facilitate efficient and expert mentorship for startups and build an outcome-oriented
        mechanism that allows timely tracking of the mentor-mentee engagements.
   •    It is National Mentorship Platform by Startup India.

NIRYAT portal

   •  NIRYAT stands for National Import-Export for Yearly Analysis of Trade.
   •  Objective – It is developed as a one stop platform for stakeholders to get all necessary
       information related to India’s foreign trade
   •  Launch Year: 2022

Indian Business Portal

   •  Objectives
      ▪  To digitize Indian Exporters and help them become discoverable online.
      ▪  To promote exports from all Indian States.
      ▪  To showcase India’s strength in wide range of Products & Services.
      ▪  To encourage virtual meetings between buyers and sellers.
      ▪  To provide a trusted network of Indian Exporters to Foreign Buyers.
   •  Launch Year: 2022.
   •    It is an e-commerce marketplace exclusively for exporters registered in India.
   •    It seeks to empower SMEs, artisans and farmers and support Indian exporters to get global
         visibility.
   •    It gives focus on promotion of GI products from India.

   Ministry of Information & Broadcasting

e-Rozgar Samachar

      •  Objective: To make aspirants aware of job opportunities in government sector including
          public sector enterprises.
      •  Launch Year: 2019.
      •    It provides information and guidance about admission and career opportunities in
          various streams through career-oriented articles by experts.

                                                                                                                        pg. 11

[Type here]


Broadcast Seva Portal

   •    It is an online portal solution for speedy filing and processing of applications of broadcasters
        for various kinds of licenses, permissions, registrations, etc.
   •  Launch Year: 2022
   •    It provides following services and features:
      ▪  End-to-end processing
      ▪  Integration with payment system (Bharat Kosh)
      ▪  Integration with E-Office and stakeholder ministries
      ▪  Analytics, Reporting and Management Information System (MIS)
      ▪  Integrated Helpdesk
      ▪  Application forms and status tracking
      ▪  Downloading letters/orders from the portal itself
      ▪  Alerts to stakeholders (SMS/E-Mails)
   •    It provides 360-degree solution to over 900 Satellite TV Channels, 70 Teleport operators,
     1750 multi-service operators, 350 Community Radio Stations, 350 Private FM Channels
       etc.
   •    It will ensure smooth coordination with other ministries and enable analysis & reporting.

 Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

e-NAM

   •  e-NAM stands for electronic – National Agriculture Market.
   •    It is a pan-India electronic trading portal to create a unified national market for agricultural
      commodities.
      ▪    It networks the existing APMCs/Regulated Marketing Committee (RMC) market yards,
         sub-market yards, private markets and other unregulated markets.
   •  Launch Year: 2016.
   •  Implementing Agency: Small Farmers Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC)
      ▪    It is completely funded by Central Government.
   •  Objectives:
      ▪  To promote uniformity in agriculture marketing by streamlining of procedures across the
          integrated markets.
      ▪  To remove information asymmetry between buyers and sellers.
      ▪  To promote real time price discovery based on actual demand and supply.

e-Pashu Haat portal

   •  Objective: To connect breeders and farmers regarding availability of bovine germplasm.
   •  Launch Year: 2016.
   •    It was developed under National Mission on Bovine Productivity.
   •  Through the portal, breeders/farmers can sell and purchase breeding stock, information on
         all forms of germplasm including semen, embryos and live animals with all the agencies
     and stake holders.
                                                                                                                        pg. 12

[Type here]



   •    It will also make farmers aware about the availability of quality disease free bovine
     germplasm with different agencies in the country.

ENSURE Portal

   •  ENSURE stands for ElectroNic Submission of REturns
   •  Launch Year: 2018.
   •  Developed by: NABARD and operated under the Department of Animal Husbandry,
       Dairying & Fisheries.
   •  Under Entrepreneurship Development and Employment Generation (EDEG) component of
       National Livestock Mission, subsidy is directly paid into beneficiary’s account through Direct
       Benefit Transfer (DBT).
      ▪  Subsidy is paid for activities related to poultry, small ruminants, pigs etc.
   •  ENSURE portal was launched to make this payment process better, simpler and
       transparent.
   •    It will also make information related to beneficiary and processing of application readily
       available.

Farmers Portal

   •  Objective: To create one stop shop for meeting all informational needs related to
       Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Fisheries sectors production, sale/storage of farmers.
   •    It provides information about package of practices, crop and seed varieties, common pests,
      dealer network for seeds, fertilizers & pesticides, machinery and tools, agro-met advisories,
       credit & insurance, rain-fed areas etc.

mKisan Portal

   •  Objective: To leverage power of mobile telephony to reach out to the farmers and also
      address their concerns and queries.
   •  Launch Year: 2013.
   •    It is a unified platform to send targeted text and voice-based advisories to farmers on a host
       of issues related to agriculture and allied sectors.
   •    It enables all Central/State government organizations in agriculture and allied sectors to
       give information/services/advisories to farmers by SMS in their language, preference of
       agricultural practices and location.

Kisan Suvidha

   •  Objective – To provide information on five critical parameters- weather, input dealers,
      market price, plant protection and expert advisories.
   •  Launch Year: 2016.
   •   It provides following services and information
      ▪  Weather Forecast.
      ▪  Extreme Weather Alert.
      ▪  Market Price of commodities.

                                                                                                                        pg. 13

[Type here]



      ▪  Dealers - Fertilizer, Seeds, Pesticide, Seeds etc.
      ▪  Plant protection for 12 major crops.
      ▪  Agro advisories.
      ▪  Soil Health card.
      ▪  Soil testing labs.
      ▪  Cold Stores & Godowns.
      ▪  Vet Labs & Diagnostic Centres.
      ▪  Crop Insurance.
      ▪  Government Schemes.
   •    It is available in 7 languages viz. English, Hindi, Tamil, Gujarati, Oriya, Punjabi, Marathi,
      Bengla and Telugu.

Pusa Krishi Mobile App

   •    It disseminates information about the latest technologies developed by the Indian
       Agricultural Research Institute, to farmers.
   •  Launch Year: 2016.
   •    It is available in two languages: Hindi and English.

             Ministry of Finance

Vidya Lakshmi Portal

   •  Objective: To ensure that students can avail loans easily through single window system of
      banks for education loans.
   •  Launch Year: 2015.
   •  Developed and maintained by: NSDL e-Governance Infrastructure Limited in
       collaboration with Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education and Indian Banks Association
       (IBA).
   •    It provides single window mechanism for the application and disbursement of government
      scholarships and educational loans provided by the banks.

ICEDASH

   •  Objective: To help public see the daily Customs clearance times of import cargo at various
       ports and airports.
   •  Launch Year: 2019
   •  Developed by: Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBIC) in collaboration with NIC.
   •    It is an Ease of Doing Business monitoring dashboard of the Indian Customs.
   •    It helps the businesses compare clearance times across ports and plan their logistics
       accordingly.





                                                                                                                        pg. 14

[Type here]


e-B-kray e-auction portal

   •  Objective: To enhance user experience through seamless access to information by search
      based on type and location of property put up for e-auction by banks in India.
   •  Launch Year: 2019.
   •    It is a common e-auction platform to enable online auction of attached assets transparently
        for the improved realization of value by banks.
   •    It has been linked on Indian Banks Auctions Mortgaged Properties Information (IBAPI)
        portal.
   •    It promotes online auction of assets attached by the banks.
   •    It is equipped with the property search features and contains navigational links to all PSBs
       e-auction sites.

ATITHI Mobile App

   •  Objective: To improve monitoring and pace of Customs clearance of imported goods and
        facilitatign arriving international passengers by electronic filing of Customs baggage and
      currency declarations.
   •  Launch Year: 2019.
   •  Launched By: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs.
   •    It is easy to use mobile app for international travellers to file the Customs declaration in
      advance.
   •  Using it, passengers can file declaration of dutiable items and currency with the Indian
     Customs even before boarding the flight to India.

Jan Samarth Portal

   •  Objective: To encourage inclusive growth and development of various sectors by guiding
     and providing them right type of government benefits through simple and easy digital
      processes.
   •  Launch Year: 2022.
   •    It is national portal for credit linked government schemes.
   •    It ensures end to end coverage of all the linked schemes.
   •  Key features
      ▪    It connects all stakeholders like beneficiaries, financial institutions, Central/State
        Government Agencies, & Nodal Agencies on a common platform.
      ▪    It enables applicant to access 13 schemes through a single platform.
      ▪    It provides intuitive guidance to applicants for checking subsidy eligibility.
      ▪    It has auto recommendation of the best suitable scheme for beneficiary.
      ▪    It provides digital approval of loan application based on digital verifications.
      ▪    It allows beneficiary to track real time status of their loan application.





                                                                                                                        pg. 15

[Type here]


NETRA Portal

   •  NETRA stands for New e-Tracking and Remote Administration.
   •  Objective: To efficiently manage and monitor Line of Credits (LOC) and Concessional
      Finance Projects extended by Export-Import Bank of India.
   •  Launch Year: 2022.
   •  Developed by: EXIM Bank
   •    It allows seamless and secure access to information, real-time updates on project
      implementation and expeditious delivery of quality projects.

  Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

UMANG App

   • UMANG stands for Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance.
   •  Objective: To abridge inconvenience faced by citizens in managing multiple mobile apps
     and facilitate a one-stop-solution to avail varied government services.
   •  Launch Year: 2017
   •  Developed and operated by: National e-Governance Division.
   •    It is a unified platform and mobile app to facilitate a single point of access to all government
       services.
   •    It acts as a master application and integrates major government services from various
       sectors such Agriculture, Education, Health, Housing among others.
   •    It enables users to access e-Government services from the central Government, the State
      Governments, local bodies and their agencies.

Meri Pehchaan Portal

   •  Objective: It is National Single Sign-on platform to facilitate/provide citizens ease of access
       to government portals.
   •  Launch Year: 2022.
   •    It is a user authentication service in which a single set of credentials provide access to
       multiple online applications or services.

My Scheme Portal

   •  Objective: To offer a one-stop search and discovery portal where users can find schemes
       that they are eligible for.
   •    It is a service discovery platform facilitating access to Government Schemes.
   •  Launch Year: 2022





                                                                                                                        pg. 16

[Type here]


e-SamikSha

   •  Launch Year: 2014.
   •    It is a real time, on-line system for monitoring of follow-up action on the decisions taken
      during the presentations made by different Department/Agency to the Prime Minister.
   •  The follow-up action in respect of each decision is updated on it by the concerned Ministry/
      Department/ Agency as and when the status changes or at least every month.
   •    It can be securely accessed by different users such as the PMO/ Cabinet Secretariat/
       Ministries/ Departments through a Log-In/ Password.
   •    It can be also configured to review the follow up action in respect of other meetings, if
       required.

MyGov Portal

   •  Launch Year: 2014.
   •    It is Government of India’s Citizen Engagement Platform which collaborates with multiple
     Government bodies/ Ministries to engage with citizens for policy formulation and seeks the
      opinion of people on issues/ topics of public interest and welfare.
   •    It is used by Government Departments for their citizen engagement activities, consultations
        for policy formulation and also to disseminate information to citizens for various
     Government schemes and programs.
   •    It is part of Digital India Corporation, a Section 8 company under Ministry of Electronics and
       IT

              Ministry of MSME

CHAMPIONS Portal

   •  CHAMPIONS stands for Creation and Harmonious Application of Modern Processes for
       Increasing the Output and National Strength.
   •  Objectives
      ▪  To help MSMEs to resolve problems in areas of finance, raw materials, labour,
          permissions, etc.
      ▪  To help MSMEs capture new opportunities in manufacturing and services sectors.
      ▪  To identify sparks, i.e. bright MSMEs who can withstand at present and become national
        and international champions.
   •  Launch Year: 2020.
   •    It is enabled by Artificial Intelligence, Data Analytics and Machine Learning.
   •    It is integrated on real time basis with Central Government’s main grievances portal
    CPGRAMS and MSME Ministry’s own other web-based mechanisms.





                                                                                                                        pg. 17

[Type here]


SIDHEE Portal

   •  SIDHEE stands for Simplified Digital Hands-on Information on Energy Efficiency in MSMEs.
   •  Launch Year: 2019
   •  Developed by: Bureau of Energy Efficiency as part of its MSME Programme – Knowledge
     Management and Sharing initiative.
   •    It is a repository of policy focussed initiatives executed by BEE for MSME Sector,
      showcasing holistic database of BEE's initiatives pursued to strengthening MSME Sectors.
   •    It also contains information on energy efficient technologies, best industrial practices and
      success stories.

MSME SAMADHAAN

   •  Objective: For empowering micro and small entrepreneurs across the country to directly
       register their cases relating to delayed payments by Central
      Ministries/Departments/CPSEs/State Governments.
   •    It is MSME Delayed Payment Portal for effective monitoring of delayed payments.
   •  Launch Year: 2017.
   •    It gives information about the pending payment of MSEs with individual CPSEs/Central
       Ministries, State Governments, etc.
   •  The information on this portal is available in public domain. This enables to exert moral
      pressure on the defaulting organisations.

Udyam Sakhi Portal

   •  Objective: To nurture entrepreneurship and create business models for low-cost products
     and services to empower women and make them self-reliant and self-sufficient.
   •  Launch Year: 2018.
   •    It provides assistance through its platform for entrepreneurship learning tools, incubation
         facility, training programs for fund raising, providing mentors, one-on-one investor meet,
      provide market survey facility and technical assistance.

MSME Saksham Portal

   •    It is a comprehensive financial education and knowledge platform for MSMEs.
   •    It supports MSMEs in managing their credit obligations and guides them across their credit
         life cycle.
   •  Launch Year: 2020
   •  Developed by: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) in association with
      TransUnion CIBIL.
   •    It provides MSMEs quick access to finance and empower them by making them financially
      aware and loan-ready so that timely and affordable financial support is realised.
   •    It also comprises a consolidated list of all the schemes launched by the Centre and state
      governments for MSMEs.




                                                                                                                        pg. 18

[Type here]


UDYAM Registration Portal

   •  Launch Year: 2020
   •    It is an online system for registering MSMEs.
   •    It is fully online, does not require any documentation, and is a step towards Ease of Doing
      Business for MSMEs.
   •    It is linked to the databases of the Central Board of Direct Taxes and Goods and Services
     Tax Network. 

MSME Sambandh

   •  Objective: To monitor the implementation of the Public Procurement from MSMEs by
       Central Public Sector Enterprises.
   •  Launch Year: 2017.

  Ministry of Women and Child Development

GHAR - GO Home and Re-Unite Portal

   •  National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has launched GHAR - GO
    Home and Re-Unite portal for restoration and repatriation of Child.
   •  Launch Year: 2022
   •  Objective: To address the amended roles of Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) and
        District Child Protection Officers (DCPOs) in matters of children in need of care and
       protection.

Features GHAR - GO Home and Re-Unite
   •   Digital tracking and monitoring of children who are in the juvenile justice system and have
       to be repatriated to another Country/State/District.
   •   Digital transfer of cases of children to the concerned JJB/CWC of the State. It will help in
      speedy repatriation of children.
   •    It will ensure proper restoration and rehabilitation of children by digitally monitoring the
      progress of the case of the child.
   •  Provide list of government implemented schemes to enable CWCs to link the child with
      these schemes to strengthen the family and ensure that child remains with his/her family.

Khoya Paya web portal

   •    It is a citizen-based website to exchange information on missing and found children.
   •  Launch Year: 2015.
   •  Developed by: Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Department of
       Electronics and Information Technology.
   •    It is an enabling platform, where citizens can report missing children, as well as sightings of
        their whereabouts without wasting much time.


                                                                                                                        pg. 19
